stemMd: Which observation would most strongly justify checking for an upstream blockage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Visitors read the new explanatory sign

options.label: B
options.textMd: The channel is dry after a long rainless period

options.label: C
options.textMd: Plants grow along the channel edge

options.label: D
options.textMd: The channel stays dry after substantial rain when flow would be expected

options.label: E
options.textMd: The basin is visible from a path

explanationMd: The suspected fault depends on a mismatch between expected and observed operation. After substantial rain, continued dryness may indicate that water is not reaching the channel. Dryness without rainfall lacks that implication.

distractorRationale.b: That is the normal dry-weather condition described.
distractorRationale.a: Reading does not indicate a hydraulic fault.
distractorRationale.c: The channel was designed to be planted.
distractorRationale.e: Visibility alone does not indicate blockage.
